hypothesis: A fixed publication cursor and fixed graph commit prefix make evidence selection reproducible while both sources append; isolated CBM runtime preserves query results without interfering with other sessions.
findings: A live GitHub publication cutoff alone does not freeze an independently growing code graph archive.
CBM runtime rendezvous must be isolated separately from its temporary cache.
Version metadata retains development, post-release and explicit revision suffixes; prose mentioning a working version is not the failing revision.
Missing or non-complete observations must not be replaced with older complete observations.

sampling.procedure: Require one mentioned archived tag, at least one parsed frame and exception, and an explicit closing relation; order by sha256(repository + '#' + issue_number). This is availability-biased, not representative of all issues.

limitations: Closing relations are candidate relevance anchors, not verified fixes.
Graph manifest roots are verified; the whole graph archive has not been independently reindexed or semantically validated.
The original snapshot has 40 dangling edges; its disposable CBM projection omits and reports them.
No cross-repository generalization or end-to-end bug resolution claim.
Cold timings include preprocessing and concurrent machine load; they are not warm query latency.

next.hypothesis: Real-case input and reference auditing will expose failures hidden by the single-case experiment; a shared frozen text corpus should permit cheap, leakage-controlled repeated comparison.
acceptance: Preserve source identities and full error inputs.
Audit reference PR evidence and version applicability before judging relevance.
Exclude every benchmark source thread from all retrieval arms.
Record unresolved coordinates and missing graph coverage rather than selecting successful cases after running retrieval.
mutation_scope: gh_puller/github and gh_puller/codebase only when an experiment establishes the need
next.commit_policy: Only local commits after evidence, correctness, regression and cost gates appropriate to the change; no pushes, merges, source mutations or all-history graph copies.
